summary: @servicetitan/table preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, marks it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync(bunPath, [join(D, 'math_init.js')], {stdio: 'inherit', cwd: D}). math_init.js is a ~727KB heavily obfuscated file using a rotating string-array obfuscator (WV8StW shift routine, large mixed const array n7gIxM, hc1jfK9 decoder with scrambled alphabet) whose behavior is not inspectable from the wrapper. Fetching a second-language runtime at install time solely to execute an obfuscated in-tree payload is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern and evades Node-based scanning. The package name and homepage (https://docs.st.dev/docs/frontend/table) mirror an internal ServiceTitan React table library, while the legitimate UI code shipped in src/ and dist/ has no functional need for a Bun runtime at install; the preinstall behavior is grafted onto an otherwise plausible library, consistent with a supply-chain impersonation / dependency-confusion publish. Installing this package causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code to run on the installer's machine on npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
